newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. A RELIEF FOR GERMAN SHARES, CAUTION PERSISTS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. A RELIEF FOR GERMAN SHARES, CAUTION PERSISTS.

text.p: German shares bounced back from the worst of their losses on Wednesday afternoon as fears of serious inflationary pressure in the U.S. were eased by softer-than-expected data for July.
"Everyone had started to expect the worst," said a dealer at a top Frankfurt bank, of a slide that saw the IBIS DAX index reach a trough of 4,237.72 points in post-bourse electronic session.
By 1250 GMT, 20 minutes after the U.S. data were released, the 30-share IBIS DAX was some 100 points higher, trading down 50.99 points at 4,326.52.
U.S. July retail sales rose 0.6 percent, against average forecasts for a 0.7 percent rise, while producer prices fell 0.1 percent, against expectations for an advance.
Dealers said the outlook for the market depended largely on the reaction on Wall Street to the economic news, which was expected to be positive.

"This market has long since stopped reacting to real fundamentals," said a London dealer in German shares, who said the market looked likely to remain vulnerable for the time being to swings and shifts across the Atlantic, as the traditional summer lull continues to keep volumes modest.
"People are still going to be cautious with more data due," he added.
U.S. data scheduled for release on Thursday includes jobless claims and consumer prices.

Another possible pressure on prices would come from persistent talk of an imminent German interest rate hike, accelerated by the Bundesbank's warnings over inflation in its monthly report released on Wednesday.
At the same time, dealers said a minor rate hike had been factored in at this stage.
Losses were generally spread across the board with chemical giant Hoechst AG, which earlier said it expected its profits this year to be below year-ago levels, trading down 2.30 marks at 82.50 marks.
Smaller rival Henkel KGaA bucked the trend, on the other hand, to trade up 70 pfennigs at 107 marks as it continued to benefit from well-received interim earnings released on Tuesday.
Attention will remain on the chemical sector, with BASF AG due to release its six month earnings on Thursday.
